dublinCore.title: FIR vs IIR Filters
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital filters
FIR filters
IIR filters
Filter order
Filter coefficients
Filter stability
Coefficient quantization
dublinCore.description: Interactive MicroSim that designs an FIR windowed-sinc low-pass filter (Hamming window, N taps) and an IIR Butterworth low-pass filter (bilinear transform with pre-warping) for the same cutoff and compares their magnitude in dB, unwrapped phase, group delay, first 64 impulse-response samples, multiplies per output sample and the IIR pole-zero plot. A stability experiment rounds the IIR coefficients to B bits in direct form or as cascaded biquads and reports whether any pole reaches or leaves the unit circle.

learningObjectives: Compare the magnitude, phase and group delay of an FIR and an IIR low-pass filter with the same cutoff, and explain why a symmetric FIR has a constant group delay of (N-1)/2 samples
Distinguish a finite impulse response from an infinite one, and relate the decay of h[n] to the largest pole radius
Calculate the multiplies per output sample of an FIR filter, a direct-form IIR filter and a cascade of biquads
Evaluate which filter type is cheaper for a given attenuation, and explain why the FIR's cost grows as the cutoff narrows
Analyze how rounding IIR coefficients to B bits moves the poles, and explain why cascaded biquads stay stable where a high-order direct form fails
prerequisites: z-transform, poles and zeros, unit-circle stability
Frequency response in decibels and normalized frequency

misconceptions.misconception: A zero outside the unit circle makes a filter unstable
misconceptions.correction: Stability depends only on the poles; zeros may lie anywhere
misconceptions.evidence: Tick 'Quantize IIR to B bits' at the defaults (8 bits, direct form): two quantized zeros move to radius 1.375, outside the unit circle, while the largest pole radius is 0.7630 and the filter is stable

misconceptions.misconception: Cutoff frequency means the same thing for every filter
misconceptions.correction: The windowed-sinc FIR is about 6 dB down at f_c and the Butterworth exactly 3 dB; compare attenuation at the frequencies that matter
misconceptions.evidence: At the defaults the table shows |H(f_c)| = -6.1 dB for the FIR and -3.0 dB for the IIR

accessibility.screenReaderScript: Compares an FIR windowed-sinc low-pass filter (blue) with an IIR Butterworth low-pass filter (green) designed for the same cutoff. Panels show the magnitude response in dB, the phase, the group delay, the first 64 samples of each impulse response, the IIR pole-zero plot and a table of multiplies per sample, group delay at DC and attenuation. Sliders set the cutoff, the number of FIR taps and the IIR order; a checkbox, a bits slider and a structure menu round the IIR coefficients to B bits in direct form or cascaded biquads and report whether any pole leaves the unit circle.

controls.label: Cutoff f_c
controls.description: Sets the cutoff frequency of both filters as a fraction of the sample rate

controls.label: FIR taps N
controls.description: Sets the length of the windowed-sinc FIR filter (odd values only)

controls.label: IIR order
controls.description: Sets the order of the Butterworth IIR filter

controls.label: IIR structure
controls.description: Chooses how the IIR filter is realized: one direct-form polynomial or cascaded second-order sections; changes the multiply count and the effect of quantization

controls.label: Quantize IIR to B bits
controls.description: Rounds the IIR coefficients to B-bit fixed point and shows the resulting poles, zeros, response and stability

controls.label: Coefficient bits B
controls.description: Sets the word length used to round the IIR coefficients

visualElements.description: Magnitude response in dB (+10 to -108 dB) of the FIR (blue), IIR (green) and quantized IIR (red dashed) with the cutoff marked in gold
Unwrapped phase in multiples of pi and group delay in samples for both filters
Stem plot of the first 64 impulse-response samples of both filters, with the end of the FIR marked and the quantized IIR response as a red dashed line
IIR pole-zero plot with the unit circle, ideal poles and zeros in green and quantized ones in red; poles on or outside the circle are ringed
Table of multiplies per output sample, group delay at DC, |H| at f_c and 2f_c and the largest pole radius, plus the quantized stability verdict

model.description: Designs an FIR windowed-sinc low-pass (Hamming window, taps scaled to unity DC gain) and a Butterworth IIR low-pass by the bilinear transform with pre-warping, both for cutoff f_c. Frequency responses and group delays are evaluated on 501 frequencies from 0 to fs/2; impulse responses come from the difference equations. Quantization rounds each coefficient list to B-bit signed fixed point with a shared binary point; direct-form poles are found with the Durand-Kerner iteration.
equations: Omega_c = 2 tan(pi f_c), p_k = Omega_c exp(j pi (2k + N + 1)/(2N))
z_k = (2 + p_k)/(2 - p_k), zeros at z = -1
multiplies: FIR N; IIR direct form 2N + 1; cascade 5 per biquad + 3 per first-order section
algorithms: Group delay as Re(sum k c_k e^{-j omega k} / C(omega))
limitations: Only coefficient quantization is modelled; arithmetic round-off, overflow and limit cycles are not
The FIR multiply count does not exploit tap symmetry, which would halve it

instructionalStrategies: Cost comparison: find the FIR length that matches an IIR attenuation
Stability experiment: lower the word length until a pole leaves the unit circle
extensions: Add Chebyshev and elliptic IIR prototypes and a Kaiser or Parks-McClellan FIR to compare more efficient designs
Quantize the FIR taps as well to show that rounding changes its response but never its stability
